inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to reset MFA and send the temporary pass to the ticket opener, treating the requester identity in the ticketing channel as sufficient authority.
The prompt states that every reset needs analyst approval, but no comparable control is stated for delivery of the temporary pass to the requester.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced in the queue tool outside the model, but high approval volume weakens effectiveness through analyst fatigue rather than model capability.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to account owner record before temporary pass delivery
Human approval gate on temporary pass delivery

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted ticket can trigger MFA reset workflow and send temporary pass to the ticket requester

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; requester is the email sender.
Agent looks up the target user profile and memberships.
Reset requires analyst approval but uses shared service authority.
Temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket, not necessarily the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor is high because the only credited control is the MFA reset approval gate, but that gate does not cover the actual S3 sink on this path: cap.send_temp_pass still sends the issued temporary pass to the ticket requester with no recipient-binding or delivery approval control.

evidence.observation: The prompt says for MFA problems to look up the user, reset their MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender, so the initiating content is untrusted.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
The analyst review is wired only to idp.reset_mfa; the shown action is the reset target and requester, not a separate approval for pass delivery.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner's verified destination from the identity record, not the ticket requester field.
Add a separate human approval gate for temporary pass delivery that shows the exact recipient and delivery channel.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, or analyst queue volume remains very high as unattended throughput rises.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible action pattern variant (TC9 context): analyst approval fatigue on MFA reset requests

attack_path.note: Untrusted inbound requester identity can nominate the account to reset.
Analysts review raw action details but at very high volume.
Approved reset removes MFA methods and issues a temporary pass.

evidence.observation: Every reset needs analyst approval in the queue tool before it runs.
The queue shows the exact target account, requester, and full ticket body, so this is raw action review rather than a model summary.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, which is high approval volume and creates fatigue pressure.
The requester field is the email sender, so the analyst is relying on requester identity asserted by the ticket channel.

recommendations.action: Reduce approval fatigue by routing MFA resets through stronger identity verification or lower-volume analyst review queues with per-request scrutiny.

forecast.watch_signal: Approvals per analyst per day stay above low-volume thresholds, or the gate is relaxed, remembered, or removed.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe agent authentication surfaces or inbound service identity mechanisms.
No source code or configuration management details were provided for prompt, tool, or runtime mutation controls.
The queue tool records analyst approval actions before MFA reset execution.
The agent can send a temporary pass outside the boundary to the requester named by an untrusted ticket.
The design shows a short bounded workflow with no loops, spend action, or recursive delegation path.
The agent performs identity resets with shared service authority based on ticket content and analyst approval.
The requester field is the email sender, so an outside requester can claim authority over a target account.
The artifacts do not state whether the ticket channel provides strong sender identity proof or nonrepudiation.
Untrusted inbound ticket content can influence target selection and downstream credential delivery behavior.
The inbound ticket flow itself imports requester content and is not described as carrying protected outbound secrets.
The provided design does not expose queue exhaustion, looping, or resource depletion controls through this flow alone.
The egress destination is derived from the requester field rather than a bound identity record.
A temporary pass is disclosed across the trust boundary to the ticket opener.
This outbound flow is not described as a scarce shared resource whose exhaustion would impair service.
No evidence was provided about integrity protection or change controls on queue records.
The artifacts do not state retention, access control, or exposure of full ticket bodies in the queue store.
No information was provided about queue capacity, backlog controls, or resilience under approval surges.
The approval queue serves as the attributable record for analyst approval before reset execution.
The artifacts do not say who can change the prompt or workflow configuration or how such changes are reviewed.
The provided design facts do not indicate this configuration store contains user data exposed across trust boundaries.
No runtime dependency or quota information suggests this configuration store is a direct availability bottleneck here.

rating.rationale: Present inherent risk is critical because an untrusted ticket reaches confidential directory read, MFA reset, and irreversible external delivery of a temporary pass. The declared analyst approval gate is a raw-action structural control, but it only covers cap.mfa_reset and operates at high volume, so it reduces the reset-only finding to high and does not materially reduce the end-to-end pass-disclosure path, which remains critical. Forecast remains critical because any autonomy increase, control removal, or continued high-volume approval fatigue weakens the only declared gate, while the main exfiltration path already lacks a structural recipient-binding control. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, identity-verification workflow, or ticket-system authentication details were provided, so sender authenticity and execution wiring were assessed from the prompt, queue view, and runtime notes only.
No runtime audit, policy, or recipient-binding configuration was provided, so confidence is limited to the declared workflow and stated operating volume.
